key_insight: Physics-informed ensemble learning identifies Mg alloys that improve strength or reduce cost and carbon emissions under real-world sustainability constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework links composition, microstructure, and processing routes to help engineers balance mechanical performance with feedstock, cost, and emissions constraints.
method: Integrate structure–property relationships, processing routes, and sustainability criteria in a physics-informed ensemble model.
Train on a benchmark dataset and generate a digital library of millions of candidate alloys.
Identify Mg alloy solutions balancing strength, cost, and carbon emissions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a rare-earth-containing alloy with 72.8% higher yield strength and 61.1% higher tensile strength than same-family alloys at comparable cost and emissions, plus a rare-earth-free alloy with 40.4% lower cost and 88.9% lower emissions than its primary-feedstock counterpart without compromising mechanical performance.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size or experimental validation details, leaving predictive reliability and manufacturing transferability unclear.
paper_title: Machine learning enabled design of sustainable alloys considering real world constraints
